item.title: ARISS News Release No. 26-51 ARISS Welcomes Daryl Young as Director of Operations
item.description: September 3, 2026—ARISS-USA is excited to introduce our new Director of Operations, Daryl Young, K4RGK. Daryl is a long-time Technical Mentor with ARISS-USA, supporting many of our direct and telebridge contacts. His responsibilities in this new role will include leading all ARISS Technical Mentors along with heading up other activities related to STEM contacts.Most recently, Daryl led our operations initiative to develop a consortium of ground stations around the world to track Artemis II [...]

item.title: ARISS News Release No. 26-52 ARISS Ascends with Fall Appointments of Krenzischek, Lebair and Tucker
item.description: September 3, 2026—ARISS-USA is pleased to announce three “people moves” that will strengthen the core functions of the organization.Ryan Krenzischek, formerly the ARISS-USA Director of Operations, will take on the newly created role of Chief Information Officer, where he and his team will manage ARISS’s websites and other backend systems to ensure the seamless, efficient and secure flow of information. item.title: ARISS News Release No. 26-44 Jackie Blumer KC9LEH Appointed as ARISS Associate Director
item.description: August 4, 2026—ARISS-USA is pleased to announce that Jackie Blumer, KC9LEH, has been appointed Associate Director of ARISS-USA (Amateur Radio on the International Space Station). Jackie is a nationally recognized science educator with an emphasis on space education. In her work as an educator, she has often incorporated amateur radio into her curriculum as a teaching tool. item.title: ARISS News Release No. 26-28 ARISS SSTV Event Scheduled for this Weekend
item.description: May 8, 2026 — Amateur Radio on the International Space Station (ARISS) announces a Slow Scan TV (SSTV) event to be held this weekend. The event is scheduled to begin Friday, May 8  at 10:30 UTC | 6:30 AM ET and end on Tuesday, May 12 at 16:30 UTC | 12:30 PM ET and using a transmit power of 10 W. item.title: ARISS News Release 25-67 ARISS SSTV Event Scheduled for this Week
item.description: November 11, 2025 — Amateur Radio on the International Space Station (ARISS) announces a Slow Scan TV (SSTV) event to be held this week in recognition of Scouting and in celebration of 25 years of the International Space Station. This event will feature 12 images that will be transmitted at 145.800 MHz using SSTV and using mode PD120. item.title: ARISS News Release No. 25-66 4 US Schools/Organizations Moved Forward in ARISS Selection Process
item.description: Nov. 7, 2025: Amateur Radio on the International Space Station (ARISS) is pleased to announce the US schools/host organizations newly selected for 2026 ARISS contacts. A total of 4 of the submitted proposals during the recent proposal window have been accepted to move forward in the processes of planning to host a scheduled amateur radio contact with crew on the ISS.
